lines.trans: From today on, I am handing over this duty to you like passing down the key to the family granary.
A mission, sir?
During editing, the single most important job of the youngest producer is ordering late-night meals for the seniors.
I carried this binder for a year and a half so it feels bittersweet—do a good job!
Seafood black-bean noodles for Joon-mo, dumpling soup for Il-yong, and egg-roll gimbap for writer Ji-yeon.
Ugh, they do this every time—why can they not order from one place!
And mushroom cream risotto for Senior Hyung-geun!
Your seafood black-bean noodles are here!
Did you order from Beardy's?
Look at this—the noodles are all soggy and falling apart!

meanings.note: Emphasizes a change of state or that a new moment has arrived (contrasting with 지금 'right this second').

examples.trans: I have to go home now.
The performance is starting very soon now.

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.

examples.text: 이제부터 내가 곶간 열쇠 넘겨주는 심정으로 임무를 넘겨줄게.
examples.trans: From today on, I am handing over this duty to you like passing down the key to the family granary.
Here the word for 'storehouse, granary' is key.

examples.text: 이제부터 내가 곶간 열쇠 넘겨주는 심정으로 임무를 넘겨줄게.
examples.trans: From today on, I am handing over this duty to you like passing down the key to the family granary.
Here the word for 'key' is key.

examples.text: 이제부터 내가 곶간 열쇠 넘겨주는 심정으로 임무를 넘겨줄게.
examples.trans: From today on, I am handing over this duty to you like passing down the key to the family granary.

examples.text: 이제부터 내가 곶간 열쇠 넘겨주는 심정으로 임무를 넘겨줄게.
examples.trans: From today on, I am handing over this duty to you like passing down the key to the family granary.

examples.text: 내가 너한테 특수한 임무를 줄 거거든, 네가 들은 걸 준모도 들었는지 알아내는 임무.
examples.trans: I am giving you a special mission—finding out whether Joon-mo also heard what you heard.
Here the word for 'mission' is key.
Let's must edit together today.
I worked hard to must edit yesterday too.

meanings.note: Often used as a bound noun after -(으)ㄹ to mean 'when' or 'while'.

examples.trans: Call me when you have time.
I lived in this neighborhood when I was young.
Did you hear about this youngest member?
I was busy today because of youngest member.

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?
We are holding a meeting today.

meanings.note: Sino-Korean numeral used with counters and in numbers

examples.trans: Let's meet in the first-floor lobby.

examples.text: 일 호선이 가장 오래된 지하철 노선이에요.
examples.trans: Line 1 is the oldest subway line.

meanings.note: Bound noun placed after another noun to indicate an ongoing activity or time period, usually followed by 에 (중에). RR: jung.

examples.trans: I am in a meeting right now.
Please do not make phone calls during class.

examples.text: 여기가 바로 편집실이다, 앞으로 네가 가장 많은 밤을 새우게 될 곳이지.
examples.trans: This right here is the editing room—the place where you will pull the most all-nighters from now on.
Here the word for 'the most' is key.
Health is the most important thing.
There is an important meeting today.

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.

meanings.note: Someone who started earlier than you.

examples.trans: school senior
My senior bought me a meal.

examples.text: 편집할 때 막내가 할 일 중 가장 중요한 게 선배들 야식 넣어드리기야.
examples.trans: During editing, the single most important job of the youngest producer is ordering late-night meals for the seniors.
Here the word for 'late-night meal' is key.

examples.text: 편집할 때 막내가 할 일 중 가장 중요한 게 선배들 야식 넣어드리기야.
examples.trans: During editing, the single most important job of the youngest producer is ordering late-night meals for the seniors.
This expression comes from 'is delivering meals (humble)'.

examples.text: 나 십 년 동안 시키는 대로 다 했잖아요.
examples.trans: For ten years, I did everything you told me to do.

examples.text: 이십 년 넘게 친구 설정으로 지냈는데 쉽진 않겠지.
examples.trans: You lived as friends for over twenty years, so changing that won't be easy.

examples.text: 일 년 반 갖고 있었던 건데 진짜 시원섭섭하다, 잘해라!
examples.trans: I carried this binder for a year and a half so it feels bittersweet—do a good job!
Here the word for 'and a half' is key.

meanings.en: to have, to possess, to take

examples.trans: I have money on me.
Please bring that here (take it and give).

있다.gloss: to exist, to have, to stay

meanings.en: to exist, to be (in a place)

meanings.note: Marks the possessed item with 이/가.

examples.trans: Do you have time?
Nobody is at home.

related.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.note: Everyday spoken intensifier; can also function as a noun meaning 'the real thing'.

examples.trans: I'm really busy today.
Is that really delicious?

examples.text: 일 년 반 갖고 있었던 건데 진짜 시원섭섭하다, 잘해라!
examples.trans: I carried this binder for a year and a half so it feels bittersweet—do a good job!
This expression comes from 'feels bittersweet'.
Study well.
You did well.

examples.trans: Seafood black-bean noodles for Joon-mo, dumpling soup for Il-yong, and egg-roll gimbap for writer Ji-yeon.

meanings.note: Expresses sudden realization, surprise, or hesitation.

examples.trans: Ah, yes.
Oh, I see!

meanings.note: Used with holding or closing actions.

examples.trans: Definitely contact me tomorrow.
Please close the door tightly.

이러다.gloss: to do this, to act like this

meanings.en: to do this, to act like this

examples.trans: Why are you acting like this?
Please don't do this.

examples.trans: one person
one hour

meanings.en: to make someone do, to assign work

examples.trans: The team leader assigned this work to me.
Shall we order pizza for dinner?

meanings.en: to come (of a feeling, state, or weather)
meanings.note: Used in expressions like 혼란이 오다 (confusion comes) or 비가 오다 (rain falls)

examples.text: 한국에 온 지 일 년 됐어요.
examples.trans: It's been one year since I came to Korea.
I suddenly started feeling sleepy.
Did you order from Beardy's?
Here the word for 'from Beardy's shop' is key.

meanings.note: Demonstrative pronoun for something near the speaker; often contracted to 이거 in speech.

examples.trans: Did you film this too?
How much is this?

보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
I took the driver's license exam.

meanings.note: Placed before the verb it modifies.

examples.trans: I finished all my homework.
I ate all the rice.
Look at this—the noodles are all soggy and falling apart!
This expression comes from 'got soggy and swollen'.

examples.text: 지금 여기가 전화가 잘 안 터져 가지고요.
examples.trans: Cell reception does not really get through out here right now.

examples.text: 이번 일은 꼭 잘 해결해 봐요, 터지다는 마음으로요.
examples.trans: Let's make sure we handle this well (get through (signal)).

examples.trans: I meet a friend.
